summary: The training-domain checks used three different methods, each wrong in its own way: a min/max box in the surrogate check, a Mahalanobis threshold calibrated on the points it was fit on in training, and a per-feature box plus zero-substitution at inference.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the script's first release: a per-feature box and nearest-neighbour spacing from the start
the first release of the trainer's stored domain and the inference domain check

observables: out-of-domain flags of surrogate queries and of inference rows
the false-positive rate a surrogate domain check reports
scores given to rows with non-finite inputs
impact.bias: a broken linear constraint (f3 = f1 + f2) was never flagged, since it has zero distance along the null direction of a threshold fit on train+val; the per-feature box flagged about 10% of fresh in-distribution rows at d = 32, n = 600 against a nominal 0.1%; with replicated design points the reported surrogate false-positive rate was 4% while 100% of fresh points were flagged; non-finite rows were scored with 0 substituted
impact.trigger: correlated or constrained features, many features, replicated design points (grouped data) in a surrogate check, or rows with NaN or infinite inputs

remedy: retrain (the checkpoint stores the domain model) or rerun check_surrogate_domain.py and inference.py with a release that has the fix; rows newly flagged were extrapolations
